A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reasoning Cache work. All 43 pages of each version, including Appendices A-N, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, hard-problem experiments, scaffold comparisons, and computational-efficiency measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised IMO-AnswerBench evaluations, including updated results in Table 1 and Figures 8 and 11-13.

M1.justification: The alternating reasoning and summarization procedure, summary-conditioned RL objective, replay buffer, and two-stage training method are unchanged. Equations 5.1-5.3 and 6.1 and the appendix prompts retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Training retains AceReason-Math and DAPO; evaluation retains AIME 2025, HMMT 2025 November, IMO-AnswerBench, FrontierScience, and the hard Omni-MATH subset. The newly cited proofwriting work does not constitute an added experiment by this paper.

E2.justification: Appendix K, Table 4 removes the IMO-AnswerBench comparison against Budget Forcing, whose v1 score was 36.7. Budget Forcing remains evaluated on the other three benchmarks. Table 1's comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 7 replaces math-verify scoring of IMO-AnswerBench with the benchmark's LLM-judge procedure, using Gemini-3-Flash instead of the official procedure's Gemini-2.5-Pro. This substantively changes correctness assessment across a principal benchmark and related appendix comparisons. Training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B revises the sequential-versus-parallel compute analysis: Figure 12 replaces the dense per-turn accuracy and Maj@16 curves with rescored results at five budgets. Its qualitative conclusion remains. The summary-detail, training-turn, replay-buffer, summarization-training, and hard-problem analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: There are no added or revised seed disclosures, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3 retains the same mean and 5th-95th-percentile token-usage reporting.

E6.justification: IMO-AnswerBench results are extensively revised: Table 1 changes RCT-4B from 49.4 to 58.0, the base model from 33.5 to 40.9, and Qwen3-4B-Thinking from 49.0 to 53.8. Figure 11 reverses RCT-4B's ranking against gpt-oss-20B, which changes from 48.3 to 61.5. Figures 8, 12, and 13 also change; Figure 13 drops the 384k-512k results. These are results under revised grading, not same-protocol performance gains. Other benchmark table scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, decoding definitions, GRPO formulation, and Appendix F compute and memory derivations are unchanged. The added explanation of majority-voting token costs introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The introduction revises its specific large-model superiority claims on IMO-AnswerBench: it adds Qwen3-235B and names Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, while dropping the claim of surpassing gpt-oss-20B. The central contributions concerning extrapolation, short-horizon training, and scaffold transfer remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now cites QED-Nano as evidence that RC training can benefit specialist reasoning models, replacing v1's future-work treatment of that possibility. The new evaluation footnote attributes earlier IMO-AnswerBench underestimation to answer-format parsing failures. Appendix E's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 identifies math-verify for AIME/HMMT, supplies its access link, and names the replacement IMO judge. It also explicitly identifies HMMT November as Table 2's benchmark and explains that Maj@16 uses 16 times the plotted sequential token budget. Hardware, training hyperparameters, prompts, and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds QED-Nano and Rethinking Thinking Tokens: LLMs as Improvement Operators. Section 2 expands the comparison with parallel-trace aggregation and summary distillation, emphasizing RC's sequential extrapolation and complementary use with existing scaffolds.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of the abstract, introduction, related work, evaluation discussion, and appendix explanations. The section order, overall narrative, and appendix organization remain intact; most apparent movement results from pagination.

P2.justification: Figures 8 and 11-13 are revised with changed scales, plotted points, bar ordering, and labels. Figure 12 explicitly labels sequential compute, Figure 13 ends at 320k rather than 512k, and Table 4 loses its IMO column. Several retained figures and tables move through reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation transparency by explicitly addressing the reported answer-format grading failure, documenting its replacement judge, updating comparative claims, and clarifying majority-voting costs. These gains are limited by reduced appendix evidence and unresolved numerical consistency: Table 1 reports 46.3 for the base model plus RC on IMO-AnswerBench, whereas Figures 8 and 12 show approximately 49 at 256k. The methodological contribution remains unchanged, and higher rescored accuracies alone do not establish improvement.
